description: Self-hosted media intelligence platform: full Plex alternative + every-word-searchable transcripts. See specs/architecture.md.

entries.title: Scanner
entries.content:
Detect every video file under a library's roots, assign a stable identity (content_hash via BLAKE3 head+tail+size), and create videos rows in DISCOVERED state. Cope with renames, moves, copies, partial downloads, lying network filesystems, and 200 GB drag-and-drops.

Detect every video file under a library's roots, assign it a stable identity (`content_hash`), and create a `videos` row in state `DISCOVERED`. Cope with renames, moves, copies, partial downloads, network filesystems that lie about events, and the user dragging in a 200 GB folder in one go.

entries.title: Audio Extraction
entries.content:
Probe a video, pick the right audio track, extract mono 16 kHz s16le PCM, and feed it into the transcriber without an intermediate WAV when the backend can consume a stream. Record the chosen track in audio_tracks.

From a probed video, pick the right audio track, extract it as mono 16 kHz signed-16-bit PCM (Whisper's required input shape), and feed it into the transcriber **without** writing an intermediate WAV file when the backend can consume a stream. Record what we extracted in `audio_tracks` so the transcript can be tied back to a specific track even if the file later changes.

entries.title: Transcription
entries.content:
Convert extracted audio into transcript_segments with second-accurate timestamps. Multiple swappable STT backends (mlx-whisper, faster-whisper, openai). Per-segment durable commits, exact pause/resume, bidi-correct Arabic. The long-running stage and primary consumer of the job queue.

Convert extracted audio into a sequence of `transcript_segments` with second-accurate timestamps, supporting multiple swappable STT backends, durable per-segment commits, exact pause/resume to the audio second, and bidi-correct text for Arabic. This is the long-running stage of the pipeline (hours per video) and the primary consumer of [Epic 6](../06-job-queue/README.md)'s machinery.

entries.title: Subtitles
entries.content:
Generate well-formed SRT and VTT sidecars from finalized transcripts. Auto-discover external subtitle files. Lazily extract embedded subtitle tracks from MKVs. Streaming Service can render live VTT directly from transcript_segments.

Convert finalized transcripts into well-formed `.srt` and `.vtt` sidecars; auto-discover external subtitle files shipped with the video; extract embedded subtitle tracks from MKVs on demand. The Streaming Service can render live VTT from `transcript_segments` directly (architecture §4.5), so the **on-disk** subtitle artifacts are for portability (a Plex or VLC user opening the same folder) and for clients that prefer file URLs over manifest-embedded subtitles.

entries.title: Search & Indexing
entries.content:
Make every transcribed second searchable in two complementary ways — exact-phrase / proximity (Postgres tsvector or SQLite FTS5) and semantic (ChromaDB) — and fuse them into one ranked result set with language filters, deep-linkable timestamps, and Arabic-correct snippet highlighting.

Make every transcribed second searchable in two complementary ways — exact-phrase / proximity (Postgres `tsvector` or SQLite FTS5) and semantic (ChromaDB) — and fuse them into one ranked result set with language filters, deep-linkable timestamps, and snippet highlighting that gets Arabic right.

metadata.owner: Pipeline writes both indexes; API service reads (proxies semantic queries via gRPC Embed)

entries.title: Job Queue
entries.content:
Durable, atomic, pause-aware job queue. Single Postgres table (processing_jobs); no broker, no Celery, no Redis. All claim, heartbeat, retry, pause, resume, cancel, and reaper logic lives here. Every other pipeline epic depends on this.

Implement the durable, atomic, pause-aware job queue that every other pipeline stage rides on. The queue is a single Postgres table (`processing_jobs`, schema in `architecture §7.1`), not a broker, not a Celery, not a Redis. All claim, heartbeat, retry, pause, resume, cancel, and reaper logic is here, and is the single concern of this epic — the stages above just call into it.

entries.title: API Server
entries.content:
Go API Service. Every request that isn't a media byte: library CRUD, search, job control, settings, watch state, real-time WebSocket fan-out, gRPC client surface to Pipeline and Streaming. Stateless behind Postgres; one binary scales horizontally without session affinity.

API Server.

The Go API Service is every request that isn't a media byte: library CRUD, search, job control, settings, watch state, real-time WebSocket fan-out, auth issuance, and the gRPC client surface to Pipeline and Streaming. It is stateless behind Postgres and one binary scales horizontally without any session affinity (§1.2, §10.3).

entries.title: Streaming
entries.content:
Go Streaming Service. Every media byte: HLS / DASH manifests, range-served direct play, FFmpeg-driven transcode and remux, live subtitle muxing, sprite/poster serving, session-pinned adaptive playback. Validates JWTs offline against the API's published JWKS so a playing video survives an API restart.

Streaming Service.

The Go Streaming Service is every media byte: HLS and DASH manifests, range-served direct play, FFmpeg-driven on-the-fly transcode and remux, live subtitle muxing, sprite/poster serving, and session-pinned adaptive playback (§4). It is its own binary, shares only Postgres and the read-only media volume with the rest of the system, and validates its own JWTs offline against the API's published JWKS so it can keep an in-flight watch session alive even when the API restarts (§9.4, §9.8).

entries.title: Library Management
entries.content:
Long-lived behaviors that turn a folder on disk into a curated, browsable catalog: filesystem watching, dedup, auto-categorization, organization primitives (collections, smart collections, tags, speakers), library lifecycle, chapter inference.

Library Management.

A library is a named collection of root paths sharing a configuration profile (§5). This epic owns the long-lived behaviors that turn a folder on disk into a curated, browsable catalog: filesystem watching, dedup, auto-categorization, the user-facing organization primitives (collections, smart collections, tags, speakers), library-level lifecycle (create, scan, stats, delete-with-purge), and chapter inference.

entries.title: Auth & Security
entries.content:
Identity, sessions, signed URLs, secret handling, transport hardening. Two surfaces, one identity: web cookies + CSRF and native bearer JWT + refresh. Streaming verifies JWTs offline against the API's published JWKS. First epic to land — Epic 7 endpoints depend on this epic's primitives.

Auth & Security.

Identity, sessions, signed URLs, secret handling, transport hardening. Two surfaces, one identity (§9.8): web uses httpOnly cookies + CSRF; mobile/desktop/TV use bearer JWTs + refresh tokens. The Streaming Service validates JWTs *offline* against the API's published JWKS, so a playing video survives an API restart (§9.4, §9.8).

entries.title: Web UI
entries.content:
React 18 + TypeScript + Vite SPA. PWA-installable, RTL-first, WCAG 2.1 AA, offline-capable for everything except video bytes. Source bundle for Capacitor (mobile) and Tauri (desktop).

A single React 18 + TypeScript + Vite SPA that runs as the canonical web client, gets installable as a PWA on iOS / Android / desktop, and is the same code that ships inside the Capacitor (mobile) and Tauri (desktop) shells. RTL-first for Arabic, fully keyboard-navigable, WCAG 2.1 AA, and offline-capable for everything except video bytes.

entries.title: Mobile
entries.content:
iOS and Android apps wrapping the web bundle. Native player handoff, background download, push notifications, share targets, Keychain/Keystore for refresh tokens.

iOS and Android apps that wrap the same web bundle as a native shell, with a native-player handoff plugin, background download, push notifications, share targets, and Keychain/Keystore for refresh tokens. The web app is the source of truth for UI and routing; native code only exists where browser APIs are insufficient.

entries.title: Desktop
entries.content:
Tauri 2 wrapper of the web bundle. Native binaries for macOS / Windows / Linux. Tray, mDNS discovery, drag-drop, auto-update.

A Tauri 2 wrapper of the same web bundle producing native binaries for macOS, Windows, and Linux. Native menus, file associations, system tray, file drag-and-drop, auto-update, mDNS server discovery.

entries.title: TV Apps
entries.content:
Native tvOS (Swift / SwiftUI / AVPlayer) and Android TV (Kotlin / Compose for TV / ExoPlayer) apps consuming the same GraphQL schema as every other client. 10-foot UI, D-pad navigation, voice search, HDR pass-through, Continue Watching + Recommendations rows.

Native tvOS (Swift / SwiftUI / AVPlayer) and Android TV (Kotlin / Compose for TV / ExoPlayer) apps that consume the same GraphQL schema as every other client. 10-foot UI, D-pad navigation, voice search, and content rows tailored for living-room viewing.

entries.title: Discovery
entries.content:
mDNS LAN discovery, opt-in cloud relay (QUIC + SPKI pinning), server-to-server federation (X25519 + Ed25519 + SAS), UPnP/DLNA compatibility, QR pairing. All cross-instance features ship off and require explicit user action.

Make Maktaba easy to find on the LAN, optionally reachable from the open internet, and pair-able across devices in seconds. mDNS / Bonjour for LAN, an opt-in cloud relay for remote access, optional federation between instances, UPnP/DLNA for legacy clients, and QR-based pairing.

entries.title: Subscriptions
entries.content:
Optional premium tier (home / pro) gated by Ed25519-signed license key; free tier remains fully functional. the payment provider's (TBD) customer portal for billing; opt-in telemetry; per-tier feature flags with cohorts.

Maktaba is fully usable for free as a self-hosted single-user product. Optional premium features (cloud relay quota, multi-user seats, cloud metadata backup, advanced analytics) are gated by a license key and validated against a license server. All paid features are server-side gates; the client surface only enables UI.

entries.title: UX & Design System
entries.content:
Design tokens as single source of truth; Style Dictionary build pipeline emits CSS / Swift / Kotlin / JSON; React + Storybook component library with Chromatic visual regression; RTL-first (Arabic baseline); respect OS preferences (dark mode, reduced motion, high contrast).

A coherent visual + interaction language across web, mobile, desktop, and TV. Design tokens are the source of truth; components, motion, copy, and screens reference them. RTL is first-class; the system "doesn't have an Arabic mode", it has an Arabic baseline that LTR adapts to where required.

entries.title: Performance
entries.content:
Per-endpoint p50/p95/p99 budgets in shared/perf_budgets.yaml; warm/cold cache tags; single-flight on cold paths; embed deadline 200ms with FTS-only fallback; cache hit-rate floors; soak test detecting <1 MiB/h leak.

Maktaba feels snappy on a single Mac mini / NAS-class host with a 30 TB library. User-facing latency budgets are explicit, measured in CI on representative hardware, and regress-tested. Hot paths (search, manifest issue, range serve, WS event) hit cache; cold paths (cold transcode, cold embed) are bounded and observable.

entries.title: Scalability
entries.content:
Single-host capacity floor (50k videos / 1M segments / 30 TB on Mac mini M2); stateless API with NOTIFY+events fan-out; sticky-session streaming; SKIP LOCKED pipeline coordination; Postgres replica with lag-aware routing; bounded-memory cold scan; concurrency caps; multi-tenant readiness via flag flip.

Maktaba serves the 30 TB / single-household target on one box without falling over, and the same code paths scale horizontally to multi-host deployments without architectural rewrites. Each service has an explicit scale axis; bottlenecks are detected by load test, not by production incident.

entries.title: Testing
entries.content:
Three-tier pyramid (unit / integration / e2e) with Go build tags / pytest marks / TS suffixes; per-tier runtime budgets (60s / 8m / 12m); fixture corpus; coverage floors; contract drift fails CI; perf regression CI; flake auto-quarantine.

Every layer of Maktaba has a test posture proportional to its risk. The test pyramid is wide at the bottom (unit), substantial in the middle (integration with real Postgres, real FFmpeg, fixture media), focused at the top (a few end-to-end smoke flows). CI runs all three on every PR; nothing merges red.

entries.title: Observability
entries.content:
Structured JSON logs with required base fields; per-service /metrics with strict cardinality (no per-row labels); OTel distributed tracing with W3C traceparent + composite head sampler; /healthz + /readyz + /api/system/health; UUIDv7 error_id with rate-limited webhook; append-only partitioned audit_log; queue/job visibility; default-off outbound telemetry with redaction.

A self-hoster can answer "what's it doing?" and "why is it slow?" without attaching a debugger. Every request, job, and stream is traceable end-to-end. Health is reportable at a glance. Alerting is optional but supported. Personal data and secrets never appear in logs or traces.

entries.title: DevOps
entries.content:
Six-gate CI (lint/unit/integration/e2e/perf-ci/build-artifacts); reproducible builds via -trimpath, uv lock, pnpm lock, ko, cosign, minisign; four multi-arch container images + Caddy reverse proxy; Goose migrations with linter; SemVer tagging + CHANGELOG gate; doctor pre-flight + drain-mode rolling restart + version-jump guard; multi-platform packaging (Homebrew, deb/rpm, Capacitor mobile, Tauri desktop, native TV).

A self-hoster gets running in one command and stays running across upgrades. Maintainers ship releases predictably without manual steps. CI proves every change before it lands; CD makes shipping an already-validated build a one-liner.

entries.title: Security Hardening
entries.content:
Argon2id password hashing + RS256 JWT (15 min access, 30d refresh) + JWKS rotation (90d / 30d overlap); ACL via library_acl with JWT lib claim canonical for streaming; Caddy TLS 1.2+ + HSTS + inter-service mTLS via in-process CA; secrets precedence _FILE > env > config + log redaction; input validation including paths.canonical_under_roots; rate limits + failed-login lockout; SBOM + CVE scan gate; coordinated disclosure.

Maktaba is safe to expose on a home LAN by default and safe to expose to the internet with the documented production hardening. No secret leaves the host that wasn't authorized to. Users authenticate once and stay authenticated across the device fleet. The supply chain is auditable.

entries.title: Data Integrity
entries.content:
Atomic sidecar writes (temp + fsync + atomic rename); idempotent + resumable jobs with key (content_hash, stage, backend, model, config_hash); FK/unique/CHECK constraints + soft-delete partial unique; SKIP LOCKED + advisory locks + ChromaDB single-writer; daily pg_dump backups with verify; four DR scenarios with RTO/RPO; weekly integrity doctor; identity stability via BLAKE3 sample hash + superseded_by; forward-back compat via schema_version + cache key major prefix.

A user's media library and the platform's derived state survive crashes, power loss, partial writes, concurrent jobs, and operator mistakes. The library is the durable truth; derived data (transcripts, indexes, caches) is recoverable from it. Recovery is documented and tested.

entries.title: Cloud Relay
entries.content:
Maktaba Cloud — hosted SaaS layer (HamzaLabs): identity, server linking, WSS-tunneled HTTP relay, push fanout, provider-neutral billing (payment provider TBD), plus native installers for macOS / Windows / Linux / NAS / ARM / VPS.

Maktaba Cloud: Relay, Accounts & Subscriptions.

Maktaba Cloud is the hosted SaaS layer operated by **HamzaLabs** that turns the self-hosted Maktaba Server (Epics 01–24) into a remotely-reachable, cross-network product. It is the difference between "an app on my LAN" and "my library, on every screen, anywhere I am" — the same value Plex Cloud Relay provides for Plex.

entries.title: Content Intelligence
entries.content:
Content Intelligence: Auto-Classification, Grouping & Web Enrichment.

Maktaba can already scan, transcribe, index, and search a library (Epics 01–05). What it **cannot** do is tell the user *what* their videos are. A folder of `S01E02.720p.x265.mkv` files is, to the current product, 4 000 opaque rows in `videos`. The user still has to name the show, group the episodes, find the poster, and write the synopsis by hand.

entries.title: Live Channels & TV Programming
entries.content:
Live Channels & TV Programming.

Maktaba is, today, a **video-on-demand** server: the user picks a file and it plays. What it cannot do is the thing a cable box or Plex Live TV does — give you a set of **channels** you can flip through, each running a continuous 24/7 program you didn't have to assemble, all synchronised so that tuning in at 8:32 pm drops you 32 minutes into the 8 pm movie, the same place everyone else in the house is.

entries.title: Auto-Update (GitHub Releases)
entries.content:
Auto-Update (GitHub Releases).

Maktaba ships as a fleet of self-hosted binaries and store-distributed apps: `maktaba-server` (the unified home-server binary), the `maktaba-api` / `maktaba-streaming` / `maktaba-pipeline` services, the `maktaba-cloud` relay, the Tauri **desktop** app, and the Capacitor **mobile** apps. A self-hoster who installs once and forgets will, six months later, be running a binary with known bugs and missing features unless updating is *effortless and safe*.

entries.title: Watch Analytics & Activity Tracking
entries.content:
Watch Analytics & Activity Tracking.

Maktaba is a **multi-user** media server. An operator running it for a family, a class, or a small organisation has no way to answer the questions every such operator eventually asks: *what is being watched, by whom, when, and how far through?* Epic 29 builds that visibility in — "Tautulli for Plex, but built in" — without bolting on a second analytics service.

entries.title: Cloud Relay Anonymous Analytics
entries.content:
Cloud Relay Anonymous Analytics.

The cloud relay (`cloud/`, Epic 25) brokers traffic between home servers and their clients. As an operator of that shared infrastructure, Hamza Labs needs to answer fleet-level questions — *how many servers are connected, how much bandwidth is flowing, how are pushes landing, where are the users* — to run capacity, support, and billing. It must do so **without ever collecting individual user data**, because the relay sees traffic for households it does not own. This epic builds aggregate-only observability with a GDPR posture baked in from the first write, not bolted on.

entries.title: Multi-instance Maktaba (one home, many workers on the LAN)
entries.content: Several Maktaba installs on one local network — macOS, Linux, Windows — find each other, share one library on the shared storage (the NAS), and split the work through the queue: each machine runs the stages it is good at (the Mac's GPU transcribes, the machine next to the NAS hashes and makes thumbnails, any machine tags), with nothing to configure by hand beyond approving a machine once.

entries.title: Maktaba TV across the cluster, and remote viewing through Cloudflare Stream
entries.content:
Maktaba TV across the cluster, and remote viewing through Cloudflare Stream.

1. **One TV service across the cluster.** The home (a Mac Studio M3 Ultra, VideoToolbox) streams by default. A setting lets other machines of the cluster stream too (for example the Windows PC with NVENC) "for more users". The home balances channels across the hosts that may stream: **one encode per channel in the whole cluster**, whatever the number of viewers. The home stays the **single front door** for everything a client sees — HDHomeRun discovery (SSDP, `discover.json`, `lineup.json`, `/auto/v{n}`), XMLTV, M3U and the web app's HLS — and forwards each request to the host that encodes the channel. When a host dies, its channels move to another host and resume at the wall-clock position. 2. **Remote viewing through Cloudflare Stream.** A viewer outside the LAN tunes a channel through the Maktaba API (reached through the Epic 25 relay). The host that already encodes that channel pushes the same encoded stream (stream copy, no second encode) to a Cloudflare Stream live input; the viewer plays it from Cloudflare's edge with a short-lived signed token. Pushes start when a remote viewer tunes and stop a few minutes after the last one leaves, under limits and a monthly budget the admin sets.

entries.title: Maktaba TV staging, hot swap and change management
entries.content:
Maktaba TV staging, hot swap and change management.

Requirement: TV gets staging and hot swap. Changes go to staging; once staging is ready and live, a switch happens. So: two TV processes, a load-balanced hot swap, and an internal change management flow.

entries.title: Maktaba TV public site (working name `tv.maktaba.com`)
entries.content:
Maktaba TV public site (working name `tv.maktaba.com`).

Requirement: a public TV site (working name tv.maktaba.com; the domain is checked later) where people watch the channels through Cloudflare, as a feature next to Epic 32.

entries.title: Full-Maktaba cluster machines and automatic updates for the whole cluster
entries.content:
Full-Maktaba cluster machines and automatic updates for the whole cluster.

1. *Every machine that joins is a full Maktaba* — web UI, API, pipeline worker and, optionally, TV streaming. Opening any machine's web address gives the same Maktaba. The home stays the single source of truth: one database (the home's Postgres; machines use their own limited role), migrations only on the home, the home is the TV front door (HDHomeRun, SSDP, XMLTV, M3U, the push relay), and the Plex and Cloudflare secrets never leave the home (machines reach Plex through the service door, story 31.R). 2. *Updates are fully automatic.* The home checks for new signed releases, installs them in a quiet window (default 03:00–05:00 local) unless a check fails, then rolls the same version out to every joined machine one at a time, each verified before the next, with rollback on failure.

entries.title: Maktaba.app
entries.content:
Maktaba.app: one Mac installation that runs everything.

1. **One Mac installation runs everything.** A home Mac installs Maktaba once and gets the API, streaming (Live TV), the pipeline workers *including MLX transcription and the second listen*, semantic search, the web app, the database, ffmpeg, starting at login and restarting anything that stops. No Docker, no Homebrew Postgres, no terminal steps, no Claude-session-held processes. 2. **It is a Mac app: `Maktaba.app`.** Drag to Applications, open, follow a short setup. The window is the web app (as today); closing it leaves the server running; the menu-bar item shows status. 3. **Postgres is bundled** inside the app (≈30–40 MB for Apple Silicon), private to Maktaba, so it never clashes with another Postgres on the Mac.

entries.title: Every full node keeps a live copy of its home's database
entries.content:
Every full node keeps a live copy of its home's database.

A full node (Epic 35) used to depend on its home for everything a person does: checking a sign-in, reading the library, playing, watching TV. PR #145 made a node degrade to read-only on the home's last answers for ten minutes; PR #157 kept a playback catalog for the home's database being down. This epic replaces both with this requirement: a joined node has a passive/active relation with the home. It holds the whole database of the home, read-only and replicated at once, so sign-in, TV, playback and the rest work offline from that node, without the home's full features.

entries.title: Maktaba for Windows
entries.content:
Maktaba for Windows: one installation that runs everything.

Requirement (2026-10-20): the same one-app setup on Windows as on the Mac.

entries.title: Maktaba for Linux
entries.content:
Maktaba for Linux: one installation that runs everything.

Requirement (2026-10-20): the same one-app setup as on the Mac, on Windows and on Linux.

entries.title: Queue health
entries.content:
Queue health: a red tile means something is wrong.

1. **A tile's colour says what to do.** A stage is not red because a small share of its jobs failed. Red means *many recent jobs fail the same new way* (a bug or a bad setting). Jobs waiting on something outside them (the model, the share, disk space) are **Waiting**, and resume on their own. Items that no retry can fix (a missing or damaged file) are a **Needs you** count, not a red tile. 2. **Every failure has a class**, decided by data, not by `if`s spread through the stages: `transient`, `dependency:<name>`, `resource:<name>`, `item_permanent`, `unknown`. 3. **Parked jobs never burn attempts.** Small health probes watch the dependencies; when one is healthy again, the jobs parked on it are queued again by themselves. 4. **One page lists every failing item** — all stages, all classes, waiting ones too — with filters and the fixes an admin can make there (fix path, check permission, retry now, ignore, re-download, rescan, remove), one item or a whole group at a time, every action audited. 5. **The failures there today are moved into this model** (the 6,577 `check_tags` and 1,029 `check_clips` model failures become Waiting, missing files go to Needs you).

entries.title: Help
entries.content:
Help: a user guide and FAQ for every feature, in the app.

Requirement (2026-10-21): a user guide and FAQ for each feature, saying what to do and what it means; audit the features, build the help, and make it linkable.

entries.title: The apps
entries.content:
The apps: Player, Remote and Server.

1. **Three kinds of app.** - **Player:** browse and watch, nothing else, like the TV apps. - **Remote:** manage a home server from elsewhere: processing, transcription, settings, users, Live TV, machines, updates, and the rest of the admin pages. - **Server:** runs Maktaba itself (the API, streaming, the pipeline, the database). 2. **Which apps exist:**

entries.title: Semantic search in Postgres (pgvector), Chroma retired
entries.content:
Semantic search in Postgres (pgvector), Chroma retired.

1. Semantic search reads Postgres (`segment_embeddings`, pgvector HNSW, cosine): same results, same or better speed (p95 of the semantic leg under the API's 200 ms budget on the home Mac at full size). 2. The index stage and `chapter_infer` write and read Postgres; deleting a video, a transcript or a library deletes its vectors (FK `ON DELETE CASCADE`). 3. The 13.9 M existing vectors are copied from Chroma once, without embedding anything again; search keeps working during the copy (Chroma serves until the copy is complete and checked). 4. pgvector ships with every bundled Postgres (macOS arm64, Linux x86_64/aarch64, Windows x64) and is in CI's and Docker's Postgres; `CREATE EXTENSION vector` where the bundle creates its extensions. 5. Chroma is gone: the `chromadb` dependency, the `<StateDir>/chroma` folder (deleted after the copy is checked), the compose service, the CI service, the env vars and the docs.

entries.title: Analytics counts every way of watching, and every app's use of the API
entries.content:
Analytics counts every way of watching, and every app's use of the API.

1. **Every play of a Maktaba video is recorded, whichever app plays it**, server-side, from what every player already sends (the stream session and its progress), with the app, its version, platform and device. The web's own `/api/watch/*` calls go (one record per play, not two). Android TV keeps `/api/watch/*` (it opens no stream session) and says which app it is. 2. **Every Live TV viewer is recorded:** watching a channel in a Maktaba app or the web, through Plex's Live TV (the HDHomeRun tuner), and through the remote TV. One row per viewing, with the channel, the person when known, the surface and the client. 3. **Every app says which it is**, on every request: `X-Maktaba-Client: <app>/<version> (<platform>; <device>)`. The API counts its requests per app and day (requests, errors, time, people) and keeps it. 4. **A new analytics page** (admin): watch time and viewers across everything, by surface and app; who and what is watching now (videos and channels); trends; top videos, channels, libraries and people; the apps (people, requests, errors, speed, versions in use); devices and platforms. 5. The person's own controls stay: `user_analytics_prefs.track_enabled = false` records none of their plays or viewing (the anonymous counts of API requests per app go on: no person in them).

entries.title: Libraries
entries.content:
Libraries: manage them, browse them, and the server's storage settings.

1. An admin can see every library with its folders, counts, last scan and problems; add one (with a folder picker that browses the server's disk), rename it, change its folders, scan it and follow the scan, empty its trash, merge it into another and remove it, each with a confirmation that says what happens to the videos and their data. 2. Duplicate and nested folders are flagged on the page, with a one-click fix: merge the duplicate library into the one that holds the videos. 3. An admin can see and change the storage and discovery settings (`path_map`, `roots`, `mdns`, the listen addresses, the public URLs) in Settings, safely: validated before they are saved, saved by the server that owns the file, and applied by a restart the admin starts and watches. The page shows which library folders this machine reaches through the path map. 4. Every user gets a Plex-like way to watch: a Home page across their libraries, a Libraries page of cards, a page per library with rows (Continue Watching, Recently Added, Recently Watched, Most Watched, Series, By year) and a full grid with sort and filters, and pinned libraries in the main navigation, in the order they choose, stored on the server. 5. Every role rule is the API's, with a role test: management and server settings are admin-only; browsing shows only the libraries the user may see (`principal.AccessAllLibraries` / `principal.Libraries`), and a library they may not see answers 404, as `GET /api/libraries/{id}`. 6. English and Arabic, RTL-safe, with help pages.

entries.title: Big-screen mode
entries.content:
Big-screen mode: a 10-foot view for the couch, in the desktop apps and the browser.

1. A big-screen mode in the web app (`/big`), full screen, that browses and plays the whole library: Home, Libraries, a library, Series, a video's page, Search, Live TV, Settings and the player. 2. Every flow works with the arrow keys / D-pad and Enter / OK and Back alone; with a game controller (Xbox and PlayStation layouts, through the Gamepad API); with media keys; and the mouse still works. 3. The Epic 14 10-foot rules (story 14.3): large type, a focus ring that never relies on colour alone, rows that keep horizontal moves in the row, Back that returns to the focus it left, a 5 % safe area for TVs that overscan, no swipe-only flow, no focus trap. 4. Entering and leaving is easy and safe: a "Big screen" button in the normal UI, a keyboard shortcut, a menu item in the desktop apps, an option to start the desktop app in big screen (saved on this machine), and Back at the top asks before it leaves. 5. English and Arabic, RTL-safe (in Arabic the layout and the navigation mirror), with a help page. 6. UI only: it reads the APIs the web app already uses, and every route keeps enforcing the user's role and library access server-side (`principal.AccessAllLibraries` / `principal.Libraries`).

entries.title: Keep libraries offline, in MP4, and without duplicates
entries.content:
Keep libraries offline, in MP4, and without duplicates: three queue jobs.

- Three admin-only, queue-driven pipelines, each one or more stages in the existing `GRAPH`, run from the Queues page per library: - **A. Convert to MP4** - **B. Find and merge duplicates** - **C. Refresh from YouTube** - **No file is ever lost.** Nothing is deleted before its replacement or keeper is verified. A removed file goes to a **trash folder on the same volume** and is purged only after a grace period (30 days, see Decided). Every move is recorded in `file_actions` and can be undone until the purge. - **No user data is lost.** A converted video keeps its `videos.id`, so every row that points at it keeps pointing at it. A merged duplicate's user data is moved to the keeper before its own row is retired. - Crash-safe: a crash at any point leaves either the old file or the new file in place and tracked, and the next run finishes or rolls back the step.

entries.title: The native Players
entries.content:
The native Players: as good as the web, and as Plex.

A review of the Player apps on 2026-10-31 found five gaps: the app starts light with no theme; there is no navigation, only a libraries view, nothing like Plex; there is no TV; Epic 42 was called done anyway; and both apps' sign-in pages are bare, with no logo and no theme like the web's.

entries.title: Search that answers like Google
entries.content:
Search that answers like Google: ranked, instant, and Arabic-aware.

The plan is a plain index scan (`Order By: body <@> bm25query`, 377 buffers). At the home's size (45 k documents) the build is about a minute and the index about 0.5 GB.

entries.title: Maktaba Cloud with no downtime
entries.content:
Maktaba Cloud with no downtime: from one VPS to a relay people can pay for.

Requirement: once people pay for remote access, there must be no downtime.

entries.title: Every part of Maktaba can be turned on, off, added later or left out
entries.content:
Every part of Maktaba can be turned on, off, added later or left out.

Requirement: today every worker and feature starts right away. Each one must instead be driven by config or settings, so it can be stopped and started, enabled and disabled, with server bundles that ship with or without components, and components that can be added later.

entries.title: Word review
entries.content:
Word review: suspect words go to a person, in every language.

Requirement: transcription was chosen after hearing tests. Next, a queue job (or the step that runs the second review) reviews each transcript and saves the location of every word that is not in the dictionary, looks wrong or has low confidence, for a person to review and give the correct spelling. It must support every language, with languages added as add-ons.

entries.title: Logs, errors and problem reports from every part, and a UI that never goes dark
entries.content:
Logs, errors and problem reports from every part, and a UI that never goes dark.

Requirement: log, bug and error reporting across the server, the apps, the cloud and the API, all customer facing, with a server admin UI to view, search and analyse logs and dashboards. Every part of the server must be reportable, and no crash may break everything or make the UI unreachable.

entries.title: Plugins
entries.content:
Plugins: new functions from the queue, with no internet, from a Maktaba store.

Requirement: a plugin system for third-party queue extenders that never call the internet and add new functions by working with the queues and the Maktaba API, and a store for those plugins.

entries.title: events

entries.title: libraries

One row per transcription pass. is_active partial-UNIQUE marks the live one; history rows kept for reprocessing. Tracks backend, model, parameters, progress.

entries.title: users

argon2id password hashes; is_admin flag; failed_attempts + locked_until. Sentinel UUID 00000000-...-001 for single-user mode.

entries.title: vector_index_dead_letter

entries.title: Phase 1 — Pipeline foundations — Scanner
entries.content: Epic 1: file discovery, BLAKE3 content identity, filesystem watcher, manual control, schema decisions, video state machine.

entries.title: Phase 2 — Pipeline foundations — Audio + Transcription start
entries.content: Epics 2-3 audio extraction (probe, track selection, stream extraction, resource accounting) and the transcription backend protocol + initial backends.

entries.title: Phase 3 — Pipeline foundations — Subtitles + Search
entries.content: Epics 4-5: subtitle generation, FTS via tsvector, Chroma vector backend, hybrid RRF, incremental indexing, query suggestions, chapter inference.

entries.title: Phase 4 — Job queue + Pipeline daemon wiring
entries.content: Epic 6 durable job queue with claim loop, heartbeat, pause/resume/cancel, backoff, reaper, concurrency caps, graceful shutdown.

entries.title: Phase 5 — Subtitles + Search indexing closeout
entries.content: Phase 5 closed out Epics 4-5 and validated the cross-epic search RRF + subtitle live-VTT contract integration.

entries.title: Phase 6 — API server (Epic 7)
entries.content: API CRUD/search/sessions/settings — HTTP skeleton, cursor pagination, library CRUD, ingest endpoints, GraphQL SDL, gRPC clients to Pipeline + Streaming.

entries.title: Phase 7 — Streaming service (Epic 8)
entries.content: HLS/DASH origin: signed-URL gating, capability matrix, direct play, remux, hwaccel, gRPC session lifecycle, subtitle/chapter/poster/sprite cache.

entries.title: Phase 8 — Library management (Epic 9)
entries.content: Library config schema, multi-root overlap detection, ignore rules, periodic sweep, content-hash dedup, manual scan controls, audit log.

entries.title: Phase 9 — Auth & security hardening (Epic 10)
entries.content: User store, web/native login, RS256 + JWKS, signed URLs, single-user mode, CSRF, brute-force + rate limiting, transport security, audit log.

entries.title: Phase 10 — Web UI (Epic 11)
entries.content: React 18 PWA: library browse, video detail, player with transcript, search results, settings, auth flows. Shared with Capacitor/Tauri wrappers.

entries.title: Phase 11 — Mobile + desktop shells (Epics 12-13)
entries.content: Capacitor wrappers (iOS/Android) with native plugins for background download, file association, push, native player handoff. Tauri 2 desktop wrapper.

entries.title: Phase 12 — TV apps + discovery (Epics 14-15)
entries.content: Native tvOS (Swift / AVPlayer) + Android TV (Kotlin / ExoPlayer). mDNS discovery, QR pairing, LAN-first connection flow.

entries.title: Phase 13 — Subscriptions + UX design system (Epics 16-17)
entries.content: Local subscriptions (sources, schedules, RSS, podcast), and the cross-platform design system (tokens, components, motion, RTL).

entries.title: Phase 14 — Performance + scalability (Epics 18-19)
entries.content: Performance budgets, caching, lazy hydration, scalability targets, single-box 30TB validation, worker concurrency tuning.

entries.title: Phase 15 — Testing + observability (Epics 20-21)
entries.content: Test pyramid with tier budgets and CI enforcement, OpenTelemetry traces + metrics, structured logs, error envelopes, health/readiness probes.

entries.title: Phase 16 — DevOps + security + data integrity (Epics 22-24)
entries.content: CI pipelines, container images, migrations infra, security hardening, supply chain, atomic writes, idempotent jobs, backup/restore, disaster recovery.

entries.title: Phase 17 — Cloud Relay (Epic 25)
entries.content: Maktaba Cloud SaaS layer: identity, server claim, WSS tunnel, HTTP relay proxy, bandwidth metering, provider-neutral billing, push fanout, admin consoles, installers, entitlement signing.

entries.title: app_settings
entries.content: Runtime-editable knobs as key/value JSONB. NOTIFY 'settings_changed' on UPDATE/INSERT.

entries.title: streaming_sessions
entries.content: One row per active session. Cascades through videos.library_id. Indexed for the idle-reaper and per-user lookup.

entries.title: library_topics + video_topics
entries.content: Per-library topic centroids (k-means recluster) and per-video topic membership scores.

entries.title: library_sweeps
entries.content: One row per sweep run; new/moved/removed counts and any error JSON.

entries.title: library_stats_cache
entries.content: Trigger-maintained cache backing the < 50 ms /libraries/{id}/stats target.

entries.title: web_sessions
entries.content: One row per cookie session with CSRF token, IP, UA, expiry. Reaper-indexed.

entries.title: refresh_tokens
entries.content: argon2id-hashed opaque refresh tokens. family_id shared across the rotation chain.

entries.title: pairing_codes
entries.content: 8-char base32 device-pairing codes. state = pending / claimed / expired.

entries.title: Security architecture summary
entries.content: Cross-cutting summary: auth flow (web cookie, native JWT pair, sentinel admin token, QR pairing), JWT lifecycle (RS256 mint/rotate/JWKS/verify with kid), signed URLs, rate limits + lockout, input validation, TLS + HSTS + mTLS + TOFU, secrets precedence + redaction, supply chain, ACL roles. Cross-references Epic 10 + Epic 23 + Epic 15 + Epic 21.
